## The Mother Road

Dedicated to Angel Delgadillo, the barber who saved Route 66 when it looked like the legend would be lost to the dust of the past... and with special thanks to his stepson Mauricio. No gratitude is ever enough. I've never driven the entire stretch of Route 66. Arizona and New Mexico are parts that I revisit time and again. _I love them!_ California barely still has surviving bits and pieces. One day I'll be doing the entire thing from Motor City Detroit itself and ending on the Santa Monica Pier. I'm adding in some scenic routes like Jerome, Arizona and The Hoover Dam.

And when I do it, I'm taking my damned time.

Most likely 2029 or 2030.

\[[The Mother Road on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/37298117)\]

## Midnight 66

_aka, "At the Movies"; aka, "Diner 66"_

My fractal re-envisioning of the classic "Let's All Go to the Lobby" ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lm6IU6V-dE8)), which I remember playing at drive-in movies in my childhood and teenage years. Drive-ins are still my favorite way to watch movies... and it's friggin killing me that the last one in Costa Rica closed down right before I moved down here. That makes "Ballerina" my last drive-in movie for a bit. I'm not giving up hope. BTW, if you haven't seen the Adult-Swim retake of the classic, you're missing a hellova good chuckle. It's still up [here on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i5pb8a6SrLA).

For my own version, I took a checkered symbol fractal that I designed specifically for this, using the same melting technique that you'll see below in "Midnight Never Ends" (another favorite). Fans of _Aqua Teen Hunger Force_ spotted the inspiration, especially from Master Shake and Frylock... who somehow got himself turned into a bucket of popcorn. He probably deserved it.

Perhaps one day I'll be able to make an animated version of this one.

\[[Midnight 66 on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/55010169)\]

## Midnight Never Ends

It's no secret that I'm nocturnal by nature... ever since I was but a pup of six years. One of the few places open in the deep hours of the night, even in many small towns, are the diner shops. They've become my second home over the years as I drift from place to place. They have infamously bad coffee, so much so that when a diner actually has good coffee it immediately provokes a double-take reaction. Sadly, they're few 'n far between.

I'm notoriously a connaisseur of cafecito around the world. I can tell you that the small farms (aka, "fincas"), with small batch roasts such as from Bocanegra or Amsicia in Costa Rica are in fact the best on the planet. Years ago, my drummer, BMFD, got me hooked on brewing coffee in a French press with a touch of honey and cinnamon added to it while it steeps. This fractal is my ode to coffee culture and diner-life.

<font face="Times New Roman">_"A restaurant is a fantasy -- a kind of living fantasy in which diners are the most important members of the cast."_</font>

~ **Warner LeRoy**

\[[Midnight Never Ends on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/25256394)\]

## Quicksilver Glimmermoon

_aka, "Osram Quicksilver of the Ashanti"_

The Osram adinkra symbol, the glimmermoon of the great Ashanti Empire, set atop a black and white fractal mandala and painted in layers, dusted, then painted again atop the original fractal. The two moons form an eye when juxtaposed, looking outward from above the osram itself. Osram is the symbol of steadiness, peace, even patience... patience being a lesson that I've never fully learned. Time conquers all.

I built "Glimmermoon" atop my original award-winning fractal "Deep Space Dreamer", with that latter one featured alongside me in Marg Magazine. This time I wanted a heavily symbolic version in striking, stark black on white. The Osram itself, like a crescent moon, hangs above the blasted sands... which streak across the moons face as if clouds.

\[[Glimmermoon on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/35369747)\]

## Guy Buddha Beneath the Banyan Tree There are quite a few versions of this design floating around, with the most popular being the original "A Dream of Revolution" ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Bqm9L1Uhi9S/)) that appeared in my first art book, "[Spectral Iteration](spectral-iteration)" ([Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Spectral-Iteration-San-Jaya-Prime/dp/1367260817/)). It was my #9 Top Design of 2016, with multiple features for both the original and newer version you see here. For the new cut, I went with a more natural approach. I wanted it nearer to the feeling of the actual face of the Buddha that has grown into the roots of the tree itself in Ayutthaya. From time to time, I like to remind everyone what my true face looks like. Sometimes they forget. Humans are wont to do so. Because of this phenomena, whenever my popularity is spiking over a piece of art or music -- _or anything really!_ -- I like to post this (or a new version) to keep it fresh in their memory. Tyrants, racists, and other orthodox ismists can exit themselves stage left or stage right if they think I'll be quiet. _I came into this world seeking violence._ _"Anyone can count the seeds in an apple. No one can count the apples in a seed."_ ~**Anonymous** \[[Guy Buddha on Redubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/57535406)\]

## City of Masks

_aka, "Mascherari Macabre"_

I've never been to Venice, Italy. Not that I haven't tried... as Italy's kicked me out twice, once straight up deportation. I get it. Half the time I'm visiting a place, I'm also working "under the table" illegally. Lol, now's not the time and place for _that_ story. But the "City of Bridges" (aka, "The City of Masks") has always enchanted me. The history, the corruption, the failings that -- in the end -- in fact became a spell that fell over the city. It turns out that others feel the same way.

_<font face="Fleur De Leah">"Every time I describe a city I am saying something about Venice."</font>_

~**Marco Polo**

This is one of my earliest pieces of "pop art" fractalism, working my fractals into the mask itself. I've been told the end-effect is rather creepy for the viewer. I don't see it, so I've had to experiment. I tried out a "blue moon" version of the design. So I guess that one is both "sad" and "creepy" and very much _not_ an improvement. BUT! Every few years, someone comes long who reaches out about the design, telling me how they've gotten lost in its filigree labyrinths and caught fully within its spell.

_If that's you, then this one's for you, Love!_

\[[City of Masks on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20958434)\] \[[Blue Moon Gypsy on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/33016166)\]

## Origami Autumn

After doing collage-work with LiLi Glitch for weeks, I was inspired to take a Pythagoras tree fractal and work it in with one of these collages. Of course it had to have music in it, and autumn remains one of my favorite seasons. With those starting points, I started putting it all together. Origami paper designs became a natural addition, adding in butterflies, cranes, swans, and even a vulture... with an origami bow-tie to... lol, well... tie it all off.

It's a concept I always wanted to return to, but just wasn't a very good seller. Then came the 2020s and the rise of AI. After an existential crisis over what creativity means in the world of machines, I've pretty much abandoned being data-driven in terms of sells and art. I still make plenty of art, with almost none of it going online... writings, fractals, music, paintings.. . so much more. So I'll definitely be returning to the concept.

([Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/23856202))
